Synopsis:
    Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivered a hawkish Jackson Hole speech, driving 10-year Treasury yields to their highest since Trump's January 2025 inauguration. Warsh signaled the Fed has "work to do" on inflation and does not view current policy as meaningfully restrictive. Futures now price a ~67% chance of a rate hike at the upcoming Fed meeting. Additional inflationary pressure stems from rising crude oil prices tied to Iran war escalation. Global rate pressure is compounding, with BOJ and ECB also expected to hike. Equity futures are negative pre-market; Asian shares mixed. Broadcom earnings are the key market event ahead.

Relevance: YES — article is squarely focused on US Treasury yields, Fed policy direction, rate hike probability, and pre-market equity pricing.
